name: cv-baseline-v3
hypothesis: THE ANCHOR for the cv-medium-v3 era: the simplest thing that could work, so every later result is an addition justified against it. Bare linear probe on frozen YAMNet — Dense(15) straight off the 1024-d embedding, NO dropout, no hidden layer — label_smoothing 0.2, Adam 0.002, --fixed-epochs 400 (no early stopping, no epoch selection), medium at 8 rotating folds, translation general.
conclusion:
0.330 headline (excl. quiet+faint), 0.269 inclusive, 8/8 folds scored. NOT comparable to the archived era: different annotations, 8 rotating folds instead of 5, no dropout, and a fixed budget instead of val_loss early stopping. The archived cv-baseline 0.218 is not its predecessor in any readable sense.

THE TIER BREAKDOWN IS THE RESULT WORTH KEEPING, and it is monotonic in audibility at one shared threshold: loud 0.778 (122 frames, 5/8 folds) > untagged 0.350 > background 0.322 > quiet 0.070 > faint 0.000. That is strong independent support for the scoring split — quiet buzz is caught 7% of the time and faint never, so counting them as misses was measuring a target the tool was never promised to hit. It also says the model is not broadly weak: on buzz an operator would call audible it is at 0.78.

CAVEAT ON 1_29 AND 53, the two richest folds. _background annotations are 1874 of their buzz frames (254s median duration vs ~1s for every other tier, 51% of all scored buzz seconds) and appear in no other fold. Their 0.441 and 0.429 are therefore substantially a measure of continuous background buzz, not of discrete events. Scored as buzz per Luke 2026-09-11; TIERS_EXCLUDED_FROM_HEADLINE plus resummarize.py flips it with no retraining.

1_95 remains the known failure at 0.052, with threshold -0.137 against -1.4 to -1.9 everywhere else — the jet-flyover pathology from the archived era, unchanged by any of this.

BUDGET: fold peaks scatter 116-398 and mean(last 21 epochs) - mean(e300-320) is -0.003 to +0.013, so 400 is not obviously short. This is NOT last era, where every fixed-budget run was still climbing at its cap. The ladder is still worth one run to set the era budget, but it is no longer urgent.

name: context-verify
hypothesis: Re-verify E3's context-embedder result (yamnet_context, concat of real neighbouring-frame audio, IDEAS item 1a) against the cv-medium-v3 era anchor: 8 rotating folds, --fixed-epochs 400, --dropout 0, sensitivity_exclquiet headline. No code changes -- yamnet_context is a standalone embedder already on main; re-extracted fresh for the current annotations, then trained under the anchor's exact config with embedder swapped.
conclusion: Confirmed and larger than the E3 lead: 0.330 -> 0.415 exclquiet (+0.085), 0.269 -> 0.341 inclusive (+0.072). 6/8 folds up. untagged (+0.090) and loud (+0.092) tiers both moved as much as the headline, so this is a real detection gain, not a quiet-buzz shuffle -- passes the pre-registered falsifier. 1_150 (hard fold, low-SNR positives) moved +0.077 entirely on its untagged column, a genuine audible-buzz gain there. 1_95 (jet-flyover hard fold) got worse (-0.035, on untagged), consistent in direction with context-embedder's own E3 result at that fold; plausible mechanism is that concatenating real temporal neighbours reinforces the jet's own sustained-event structure the same way it reinforces genuine sustained buzz. 1_114 (new this era) also down (-0.083), no mechanism proposed. yamnet_context should be a serious candidate representation for the next structural comparisons (1c's hidden head, item 2's Perch concat) rather than plain yamnet.
amended: 2026-09-13 (context-frames-fix): TRUST DOWNGRADED TO artifact. The yamnet_context cache this run trained on was not built from contiguous audio. 02_set/extract.py on main never implemented the context_frames path the embedder's docstring describes -- it buckets frames by collapsed label and embeds the concatenation, so each frame's 'temporal neighbours' were same-label frames (left(i)==centre(i-1) for 98.5% of in-pickle rows; only 65.8% of ins_buzz in-pickle adjacencies were truly contiguous audio). That is context-stack's leak. Re-extracted honestly and rerun under this entry's exact config, yamnet_context scores 0.360, not 0.415: +0.030 +/- 0.015 over the anchor rather than +0.085, with 6/8 folds down against this run. The falsifier verdict also inverts -- untagged and loud move +0.018/+0.015 honestly, not +0.090/+0.092, so this is not the detection gain claimed here; the surviving gain is background-tier at the rich folds and every hard fold is flat or down. Measurement was correct for the cache it was given; the cache was wrong. Superseded by context-frames-fix.

name: yamnet-aves-verify
hypothesis: Re-verify IDEAS.md item 1b's E3 yamnet_aves result (YAMNet+AVES 1792-d concat, +0.025 honest, only intervention to ever move 1_95) against the cv-medium-v3 era anchor: fresh extraction under current annotations, 8 rotating folds, --fixed-epochs 400, --dropout 0, sensitivity_exclquiet headline.
conclusion: Confirmed at almost the same magnitude as E3 (+0.025 -> +0.024): 0.330 -> 0.354 exclquiet, 0.269 -> 0.283 inclusive, 7/8 folds up. 1_95 (jet-flyover) moved +0.046 (0.052 -> 0.098) on its untagged column -- the 4th confirmation across two eras that yamnet_aves is the only intervention to move that fold, still near chance but a repeatable result nothing else touches. untagged tier up in 7/8 folds carrying it (only 1_114 down) and background up in both folds carrying it -- real detection gain, not a quiet-buzz shuffle. loud tier down pooled (0.778->0.704) but thin (115-122 frames, concentrated in 2-3 folds) -- read as noise, flagged not hidden. 1_114 (new this era, no E3 precedent) down -0.094 on untagged, no mechanism proposed. yamnet_aves is now a confirmed structural gain alongside yamnet_context (+0.085); item 1c's wide hidden head should be tested against both before combining.

name: hidden-head-verify
hypothesis: IDEAS item 1c: re-verify E3's yamnet-aves-head-fixed result (1024-wide ReLU hidden layer, +0.030 over linear on yamnet_aves at matched budget) against the cv-medium-v3 anchor. Plain YAMNet only, per LOOP.md change-one-thing -- E3's number was measured on yamnet_aves, not YAMNet.
conclusion: +0.012 headline (0.330->0.342), inside ~0.027 MDE. 5/3 folds up/down. Hard folds split: 1_150 (positives-hard) went DOWN -0.053 on its untagged column; 1_95 (jet fold) barely moved +0.010. The one consistent tier move (background +0.058) is concentrated in 1_29/53, the two folds whose sensitivity is substantially continuous-drone detection rather than discrete buzz. Does not reproduce E3's +0.030, consistent with that number being yamnet_aves-specific rather than a property of the hidden layer itself. No stopping-rule confound (both arms --fixed-epochs 400). Read as 'no clear effect on plain YAMNet' -- the hidden head's real test is on top of yamnet_context/yamnet_aves, queued next.

name: hidden-context-verify
hypothesis: IDEAS item 1c, second leg: --hidden 1024 on top of yamnet_context (era's best confirmed embedder, +0.085) rather than plain YAMNet, since E3's yamnet-aves-head-fixed lead was measured on a concat. Matched control is context_verify_v1, not cv_baseline_v3.
conclusion: Headline dead flat: 0.415->0.416 (+0.001). 5/3 folds down/up. The two named hard folds moved in OPPOSITE directions: 1_150 down -0.047 (entirely on untagged -- same fold, same tier, same direction as the plain-YAMNet leg's -0.053, two independent runs now agree the hidden head specifically costs this fold; confirmed 1_150 has zero ins_buzz_pollination tags, its buzz is plain flight/foraging sound, not sonication), 1_95 up +0.041 (also on untagged, quiet unchanged). Pooled background tier down -0.041 (1_29/53 both down), untagged flat +0.010, loud/faint too thin to read. Combined with hidden-head-verify (plain YAMNet, +0.012, also null, also negative at 1_150), the pattern across two representations is consistent: --hidden 1024 reliably costs 1_150 specifically while doing nothing dependable to the headline. Did not run the third leg (yamnet_aves) this session -- stopping per instruction. --hidden's case is weak on both representations tested so far.
amended: 2026-09-13 (context-frames-fix): TRUST DOWNGRADED TO caveated. Both arms of this comparison were trained on the leaky yamnet_context cache (see context-verify's amendment), so the absolute numbers (0.415/0.416) are inflated by ~0.055 and are not comparable at face value to anything trained on the honest cache. The DELTA is internally matched -- both arms carried the same leak -- so '--hidden 1024 adds nothing on top of yamnet_context' probably stands, but it was measured on a representation that no longer exists, and the 1_150 claim rests on one fold at a ~0.04 delta SD. Do not quote 0.416 as an era number. Honest yamnet_context is 0.360 (context-frames-fix); --hidden on top of it is unmeasured.

name: hidden-aves-verify
hypothesis: IDEAS item 1c, third leg: --hidden 1024 on top of yamnet_aves, the era's other confirmed structural gain. Prior two legs (plain YAMNet, yamnet_context) were both null and both cost 1_150 specifically.
conclusion: +0.022 headline (0.354->0.376), 6/8 folds up. Replicated at +0.031 by hidden-aves-verify-r2; pooled ~+0.027 against a headline delta SD of ~0.012 (eval sampling), so --hidden 1024 on yamnet_aves is a real, modest positive. AMENDED 2026-09-13 twice: the baseline field said cv-baseline-v3 while quoting yamnet-aves-verify's numbers (the matched control, and the correct comparator); and the 'both hard folds moved up together' framing claimed more than a per-fold number can carry. 1_150 +0.061 +/-0.041 and 1_95 +0.051 +/-0.020 are each one draw from a distribution wider than the effect -- weak evidence for, not a mechanism. Trust restored to clean: the measurement was right, only the per-fold story overreached. Item 1c closed.
amended: 2026-09-13: repeat draw (hidden-aves-verify-r2) shows the 1_150 hard-fold gain (+0.061) did not replicate -- r2 measured 1_150 at -0.044 vs the same control, a 0.105 draw-to-draw swing on that fold alone. The headline direction DID replicate (+0.022, then +0.031, pooled ~+0.027 -- right at MDE), and 1_95 stayed positive both draws (+0.051, +0.022) though smaller the second time. Read as: a real but modest headline gain, hard-fold-coherence claim was a one-draw artifact on 1_150 specifically. See hidden-aves-verify-r2 for the full comparison.

name: dropout-verify
hypothesis: IDEAS item 1d: Dropout(0.2) was hardcoded for three eras and never tested against the current head/data/fixed-budget anchor (--dropout 0). One run at --dropout 0.2 on plain YAMNet settles whether it helps, hurts, or does nothing.
conclusion: Dead flat: 0.330->0.329 (-0.001), 0.269->0.270 inclusive, 4/8 folds up 4/8 down -- perfectly split, no directional signal. Dropout(0.2) did nothing measurable on YAMNet at this budget. Consistent with the sparsity argument in 03_train/CLAUDE.md (mild regularisation on an 89.6%-sparse non-negative code); does not test the AVES/Perch half of that claim. Settles item 1d.

name: binary-control
hypothesis: IDEAS item 12: general/binary translation control, with ins_buzz's pos_weight pinned to its general-pool value (recomputed fresh: 0.265, not IDEAS.md's stale 0.76) to remove the ~5.4x weight confound build_weights introduces via class count. Free prediction: with the head decoupled (Dense(15), no hidden layer), W[:,buzz] only ever sees gradient from the ins_buzz term, so this should come back near null.
conclusion: Near null as predicted: 0.330->0.324 (-0.006), 0.269->0.265 inclusive, 6/8 down 1 up 1 flat, largest single-fold delta -0.035 (1_150), well inside ~0.027 MDE on the headline. Confirms the decoupled-head arithmetic -- collapsing 14 auxiliary classes into one nonbuzz bucket costs nothing once the weight confound is removed, consistent with shared-trunk-head's null. Settles item 12: general/binary is not a lever on this metric under the current head.

name: hidden-aves-verify-r2
hypothesis: Repeat draw of hidden-aves-verify: is the +0.022 headline and the both-hard-folds-up pattern (1_150 +0.061, 1_95 +0.051) real or a lucky draw? No seed control exists, so an independent rerun of the identical config is the only check.
conclusion: Repeat draw: +0.031 headline (0.354->0.385) against r1's +0.022 -- direction and rough size replicate, r1/r2 differ by 0.008 inside the ~0.012 headline delta SD. Settled: --hidden 1024 on yamnet_aves is worth ~+0.027. AMENDED 2026-09-13: this entry originally read 1_150's swing (+0.061 -> -0.044, range 0.105) as proof r1's hard-fold gain was an artifact, and downgraded r1 to caveated on that basis. That was over-reading in the opposite direction from r1's own. 1_150 holds 14 buzz events, not 137 independent frames; its paired delta SD is 0.041 from eval sampling alone, and training stochasticity is larger again, so 0.105 is about one combined sigma -- ordinary, and no evidence either way. Threshold-free reads agree the models do differ on that fold (pAUC@.005 0.270 vs 0.208) but not resolvably. Neither draw supports or refutes a 1_150 story; both support the headline. The instrumentation this exposed is now in the loop: buzz_events_exclquiet in folds_sx.csv, event-blocked tools/eval_sampling_sd.py (it bootstrapped frames before, understating per-fold SD up to ~8x), and LOOP.md's rule to report per-fold deltas with their SD.

name: yamnet-aves-standardize
hypothesis: IDEAS item 9: yamnet_aves's AVES block is ~3.8x YAMNet's per-dim |mean| and 0% zeros vs 91.6%, so it may be underweighted under one Adam LR. --standardize (per-dim Normalization fit on the training pool, fold-safe, ported from pre-cutover exp/standardize-blocks) should let the optimizer treat both blocks fairly.
conclusion: Negative: -0.016 +/- 0.013 headline (0.354->0.337), 5/8 folds down 3/8 up. Both hard folds down: 1_95 -0.036 +/- 0.016 (>2x its delta SD, the more confident mover), 1_150 -0.045 +/- 0.037 (~1.2x). Epoch-budget falsifier checked and cleared: pooled late-training drift (last21 - e300-320 on val_sens) is ~0.006-0.007 on both arms, so standardization is not quietly needing more than the fixed 400-epoch budget. Likely mechanism: a linear readout can already rescale each block itself, so a fixed normalization removes the AVES block's absolute-scale information rather than fixing an underweighting. Settles item 9.

name: yamnet-pitchshift
hypothesis: IDEAS item 5: honey-bee flight (~230 Hz + harmonics) sits at the bottom edge of YAMNet's mel filterbank, where AudioSet's training mass is thin. Pitch-shift each frame up an octave (resample 16k->8k, relabel as 16k, tile 2x back to a full 0.96s patch -- frame grid untouched) before a second YAMNet pass, concat with the unshifted block (2048-d), so harmonics land in a denser part of the filterbank.
conclusion: Largest, cleanest headline gain this era: +0.069 +/- 0.011 (0.330->0.398), 8/8 folds up. Both hard folds up (1_150 +0.086 +/- 0.050, 1_95 +0.025 +/- 0.019) though individually weaker than the headline; 1_114 is the standout single fold (+0.181 +/- 0.038). Epoch-budget checked and clear (pooled late-training drift flat and comparable on both arms despite the wider 2048-d input). Falsifier (shifted block's weight norm under 0.7x unshifted AND headline inside MDE) can't bind regardless of weight norm since the headline delta is ~2.5x the ~0.027 MDE; weight norm itself not checked (CV rotations don't save weights). Standalone smoke test confirmed the shift mechanism: a 230 Hz tone's shifted embedding sits closer to a real 460 Hz tone's unshifted embedding than to itself. x4 rung not run -- left as a small follow-up.

name: context-frames-fix
hypothesis: 02_set/extract.py never implemented the contiguous-audio path both context embedders' docstrings claim it does (grep context_frames on main returns nothing -- the implementation stayed on exp/yamnet-aves-context and only the docstrings merged). Every embedder got the default path, which buckets frames by collapsed label and embeds the concatenation, so a yamnet_context frame's neighbours were same-label frames: context-stack's leak. Measured on the shipped cache, left(i)==centre(i-1) for 98.5% of in-pickle rows and only 65.8% of ins_buzz in-pickle adjacencies were truly contiguous audio. Port the padded-context extraction onto main, re-extract clean, and rerun context-verify's exact config.
conclusion: TWO THIRDS OF context-verify WAS THE LEAK. Honest yamnet_context is 0.330 -> 0.360, +0.030 +/- 0.015 -- about one MDE, and it lands on the two earlier honest measurements of this same lever (context-stack's rebuild +0.022, E3 context-embedder +0.022). Paired against the buggy run it is -0.055 +/- 0.014, 6/8 folds down. THE SHAPE CHANGES TOO, and that matters more than the size: context-verify's pre-registered falsifier was 'no movement in untagged or loud' and it claimed a pass on +0.090/+0.092; honestly measured those are +0.018 and +0.015, inside their own noise. What does not shrink at all is background (+0.132 over anchor in BOTH arms) -- the 14 long _background annotations that exist only in 1_29 and 53, i.e. continuous drone, not discrete events. Honest fold signature: four rich folds up (1_29 +0.123+/-0.042, 1_143 +0.099+/-0.048, 53 +0.076+/-0.041, 1_37 +0.069+/-0.065), all four hard folds flat or down (1_150 +0.002+/-0.040, willard -0.023+/-0.032, 1_95 -0.034+/-0.022, 1_114 -0.071+/-0.030). That is yamnet-aves-context's rich-folds-only signature, reached independently. DO NOT make yamnet_context the default representation for structural comparisons; yamnet_pitchshift (+0.069, 8/8 up) is the era's lead and is unaffected. FIX: 02_set/extract.py now pads each chunk with context_frames frames of real audio from the snip and discards the pad rows (ported from 7676e64 onto current main). Verified byte-identical output for context_frames==0 (plain yamnet over all 10 lite idents, 455 pickles, diff -r clean); new cache has clamp rate 0/3501 vs 105/3501 and a byte-identical 82842-row frame roster. STILL OPEN: yamnet_context_aves has the same mechanism -- its shipped cache is honest (built on exp/yamnet-aves-context) but predates the 2026-09-11 annotation revision, so the next main-side run would re-extract the stale idents the buggy way unless this branch is merged first. Also pre-existing on main: a clean re-extraction of ANY embedder now fails read_fold_roles on fold .../2026-07-27/1_99, which folds.csv lists but annotations.csv no longer covers; every cache on disk only passes because of an empty leftover directory.

name: yamnet-pitchshift-x4
hypothesis: IDEAS item 5, x4 rung: if the x2 pitch-shift-up rung (+0.069 this era) is directionally positive, a second octave of shift (16k->4k, tile 4x) concatenated onto the existing 2048-d cache might extend the gain. Falsifier: if it does not track x2 own hard-fold pattern (particularly 1_114, x2 standout), the win is about a shift rather than the specific octave.
conclusion: Falsifier fires: -0.011 +/- 0.007 headline vs the x2 rung, 6/8 folds down. 1_114 (x2 standout fold, +0.181 over the plain-YAMNet anchor) reverses here (-0.023 vs x2); 1_150 is the largest single mover, also down (-0.049 +/- 0.023). Tiers uniformly flat-to-down (loud 0.837->0.834, untagged 0.430->0.419, background 0.326->0.316, quiet 0.088->0.081) -- no tier-specific mechanism, just a small broad cost. A second octave of shift does not extend the win; x2 remains the best rung. Settles IDEAS item 5 in full.
